correctness.rationale: The prefix-window induction is valid: for length 2^m through 2^(m+1)−1 the word is P_m followed by a prefix of H_m. Occurrences avoiding position 2^m−1 are represented in the leading H_m, which is attracted by the previous positions. For the forcing direction an occurrence of P_r with r≥1 begins 10, so it is aligned at an even index and desubstitutes to one of the positions at the preceding level; the three starts at r=0 are 0,2,3. In the next complete prefix only the occurrence at 3·2^(k−2) has the correct predecessor for the forcing factor, whose start exceeds every previously chosen point. The length-one and length-two cases start the induction. A least-failing endpoint repairs all newly unhit factors, as each must be a suffix of that prefix. Linear recurrence follows also from primitivity of the substitution, and the optimum and ratio follow from the cited published prefix theorem. Independent check `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_examples.py 2` reproduced the first 128 symbols' greedy selections from the independent one-based v2-parity word formula; this finite replay is not the proof.

evidence: Theorem 21 of Schaeffer–Shallit gives O(A_w log N) for their greedy rule, not equality or the selected positions. Theorem 3 gives optimum two for every prefix of length at least two.
Banbara et al. describe the two minimum pairs at complete substitution lengths using one-based positions. A prefix-by-prefix greedy process does not choose such per-word optimizers.
